title: Fixed Opposed V Jaws And Two Handle Tap Wrench
description: One newly authored complete static two-handle tap-wrench exterior in a fixed empty-jaw pose. A single continuous thick rectangular head frame encloses two opposed whole V-notched jaw blocks around a genuine diamond-shaped through opening. One long fixed grip projects from the left end, while a separate coaxial adjusting-shaft appearance and complete long grip project from the opposite end. The right jaw has an integral-purpose rear cylindrical connection, and each grip has a full shaped shoulder and end cap rather than decorative detached bars. Unlike the old long one-sided F clamp, there is no offset external jaw bay, long flat guide bar or separate round pressure pad; unlike the single-handle crescent wrench, there is no side thumbwheel, tall open jaw or end hanging hole. All new mesh coordinates authored for one compact symmetric two-hand tool; no old meshes imported. One prop, zero scenes, four opaque untextured PBR roles. Empty central opening contains no tap, workpiece or actual cutting edge. Fixed overlaps are visual roots, not a validated moving thread or captured mechanism. No threading, cutting, torque, clamping, adjustment, precision, manufacturing, use instructions or safety performance. Rigging, animation and interaction not made and outside static scope.
